summary: Bio Energía Astral is a web decision-support tool for fruit growers in Los Antiguos (Santa Cruz, Argentina), a Patagonian valley famous for cherries, where late spring frosts and scarce water decide each season. Farmers draw their plot on a map, and the platform combines NASA data (POWER climate records, MODIS vegetation index via ORNL DAAC, GIBS satellite layers) with Open-Meteo and SoilGrids to compute ten-year indicators: frost risk, chill hours, water balance, slope and soil. Frost data are calibrated against the local INTA weather station and against the farmer’s own rain gauge and thermometer. A transparent rules engine compares each crop’s verified requirements (INTA, CIREN, FAO-56) with the plot’s conditions, scores cherry, strawberry, berries and cover crops, and proposes rotation strategies, always citing every data source and never inventing values. It turns satellite data that is usually inaccessible into clear, local and verifiable advice, helping small producers plant smarter, protect their soil and use water better.
details:
What does it do?

Bio Energía Astral is a web tool for fruit growers in Los Antiguos (Santa Cruz, Argentina), where late frosts and scarce water shape every season. Farmers draw their plot on a map and the system gathers 10 years of data from NASA (POWER, MODIS and GIBS), Open-Meteo and SoilGrids. It uses that data to calculate frost risk, chill hours, water deficit, slope and soil conditions. It then calibrates the results with the local INTA weather station and with the farm’s own rain gauge and thermometer. A rules engine compares each crop’s verified requirements (from INTA, CIREN and FAO) with the plot. It scores cherry, strawberry, berries and cover crops, and suggests rotation strategies.

Benefits and impact:

It turns hard-to-use satellite data into clear, local recommendations. It helps farmers reduce frost losses, irrigate better, protect their soil and diversify production. Every figure shows its source, and no values are ever invented. The approach can be replicated in other Patagonian valleys.

Tools:

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP 8 and MySQL. Leaflet, Turf.js and Chart.js. The NASA, Open-Meteo, SoilGrids and OpenStreetMap APIs. The site is hosted for free on InfinityFree and is backed by about 200 automated tests and a data audit.

Creativity:

It combines three scales of information (satellite, local weather station and the farm itself) and calibrates each one against the others. It shows uncertainty instead of hiding it. Each plot is kept private with a secret key, with no account required.

Factors considered:

The local reality: late-season cherries, frosts, alkaline soils and rural connectivity.

Data rigor.

Security and privacy.

An accessible, mobile-friendly design.

Zero cost.

A color palette inspired by the Cueva de las Manos (Cave of the Hands).

NASA ORNL DAAC: MODIS Land Products Subsets (API)
NASA ORNL DAAC: MODIS Land Products Subsets (DOI)

projectRefs: Copernicus DEM: modelo digital de elevación (ESA / Unión Europea)
OpenStreetMap: límite del municipio de Los Antiguos
INTA Los Antiguos: heladas y temperaturas críticas del cerezo (tesis Arhancet 2024, UNCuyo)
CIREN (Chile): requerimientos de clima y suelo, frutales de hoja caduca
CIREN (Chile): requerimientos de clima y suelo, frutales menores
CIREN (Chile): requerimientos de clima y suelo, cereales
Guía para el cultivo de frutillas en Tierra del Fuego (datos de INTA Alto Valle)
INTA Manfredi: enfermedades de la alfalfa (pH del suelo)
FAO Riego y Drenaje 56: coeficientes de cultivo (agua por cultivo)
FAO Riego y Drenaje 29: calidad del agua de riego
XAMPP: entorno de desarrollo (PHP y MySQL)
